title: Branch cleanup candidate record
description: One candidate branch in one cycle, stored at cycles/<cycle_id>/branches/<branch>.json on the branch-cleanup-state branch. A stale pull request is not a separate record type: it is a candidate branch that additionally carries a pull_request block, because every action the workflow takes (rename to archive/, or delete) acts on the branch either way.

branch.description: Ref name at scan time, without refs/heads/. Never starts with an exempt prefix: such refs are skipped before candidacy and appear only in the cycle's skipped list. Stored as well as encoded in the file path so a record is self-describing when read alone.

creator.description: GitHub login of the last commit's author, used by PLGQEES-2892 to group the Slack thread. Bot suffixes are permitted because renovate and dependabot own branches in this repo.

last_commit_sha.description: The restore key. The entire delete-and-restore-by-SHA model validated in PLGQEES-2888 rests on this one field, which is why it is required on every record regardless of lifecycle state.

candidate_reasons.description: Why this branch entered the cycle. Both reasons can apply at once: a branch with no commits for 90 days backing a PR with no review activity for 90 days.

pull_request.description: Present when an open PR exists on this branch at scan time, null otherwise.

decision.description: What the owner chose. Defaults to delete: absent an explicit vote or a timeout finalization, a candidate is treated as a delete.

decision_source.description: How the decision was reached. This is the field that makes the audit trail honest: silence-equals-delete produces the same decision value as a deliberate Delete click, and only this field distinguishes them afterwards. PLGQEES-2893's summary must report the two counts separately.

decided_by.description: GitHub login of whoever clicked. Null when the decision came from the voting window expiring.

outcome.description: What physically happened, held separate from decision because a decision can fail to execute: a rename collision, or the owner deleting the branch mid-cycle. Collapsing the two would make a failed deletion indistinguishable from a successful one.

archived_as.description: New ref name after a Keep vote renamed the branch. Required because the record is keyed by the original name and that ref no longer exists.

notes.description: Free text. Mandatory when outcome is skipped, so an unexecuted decision always carries its reason.

last_activity_at.description: Most recent of: head commit, comment, review, or state change. This is what pr_stale_after_days is measured against.

closed_at.description: Set by finalization when it closes a stale PR ahead of deleting the branch. A closed PR keeps refs/pull/<number>/head indefinitely, so PR-backed candidates are strictly more recoverable than bare branches.
